reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines a Log-Gaussian Cox Process (LGCP) to model spatial shot distributions and a Mixture of Finite Mixtures (MFM) to cluster players into shot-selection archetypes. The LGCP models each player’s shot locations as a Poisson process with log-intensity governed by a Gaussian process, estimated using INLA/SPDE. This yields a functional intensity surface per player. A similarity matrix is constructed using L2 distances between these surfaces, followed by Fisher Z transformation to stabilize variances. The transformed similarities are clustered using MFM, which jointly infers both the number of clusters and assignments. This dual-stage approach enables probabilistic archetype discovery without assuming a fixed number of groups. The method avoids over-clustering by using a truncated Poisson prior on cluster count and employs collapsed MCMC with Dahl’s method for partition summaries. In simulations, MFM outperforms K-means and other clustering methods in recovering true groups, while in NBA data, it identifies 9 distinct shot-selection archetypes with high stability. The framework supports downstream tasks such as predicting three-point attempt rates through improved archetype assignments.
